text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER -> SRE on-call (ashley)
incident-bot: DETECTED: org=neptune-analytics sustained token QPS spike + rising 5xx (503/504) across us-west-2 edge, error-rate > 12% last 5m. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/neptune-analytics/latency

ashley: I'm on it, paging sam & jordan. grabbing logs and current rate-limit config for that org.

sam: seeing request patterns — many long-seq completions (avg seq len 1200), concurrent streams ~130 -> token QPS jumped from baseline 8 -> 72. Backend queue depth spiked. Errors are mostly upstream 502/504 from serving nodes hitting mem pressure.

jordan: product impact? any SLA customers?

leah: support: neptune-analytics is on a paid tier but not SLA; they run nightly analytics job that started now (unknown reason). I've messaged their tech contact to ask to pause.

ashley: immediate mitigation options on table: 1) per-org QPS override (temporary throttle) 2) bump dedicated capacity (slow) 3) disable streaming for org 4) block large sequence requests (reject > 2000 tokens)

sam: we should do (1) + (4). Bumping infra will be too slow. Disabling streaming breaks their integration badly. Let's do a soft throttle first: set org override to 20 qps with 60 burst for 15m, and add server-side safeguard to reject requests with max_tokens > 1500 for that org for 10m.

ashley: agreed. will apply override and monitor. posting the admin command I'm going to run: 

```bash
# apply temporary org override via internal admin API
curl -X POST \"https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/orgs/neptune-analytics/overrides\" \\  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_SVC_TOKEN' \\  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\  -d '{"qps":20, "burst":60, "ttl":"15m", "reason":"emergency throttle - spike causing 5xx"}'
```

jordan: FYI if we block >1500 tokens the nightly job might fail. support confirm they can pause; leah says user responded "paused" 2m ago.

ashley: applying override now. ops-bot will post update once change propagated.

ops-bot: CONFIG UPDATE: applied override for org=neptune-analytics qps=20 burst=60 ttl=15m by ashley (change-id: cfg-3f9b).

sam: rolling safeguard to reject large max_tokens requests for neptune-analytics (10m). command: 

```json
{"org":"neptune-analytics","reject_if_max_tokens_gt":1500,"ttl":"10m"}
```

ops-bot: SAFEGUARD ENABLED: reject_if_max_tokens_gt=1500 for org=neptune-analytics (ttl=10m) (change-id: sg-78aa).

ashley: seeing immediate drop in total QPS from 68 -> 22 within 60s. Error rate down from 12.3% -> 1.6% over last 2m. Latency p50 improved from 420ms -> 190ms.

sam: logs show serving nodes recovered (GC and memory pressure cleared). No more 502/504. Good signal.

leah: communicated to customer: "We've applied a temporary throughput cap to protect system health; please let us know when ready to resume. We'll extend if needed." they acknowledged. :thumbsup:

jordan: what's next after throttle expires? we need a short-term plan if they rerun job.

ashley: immediate follow-ups: 1) keep throttle for next 30m if stable, 2) assign postmortem & root cause owner, 3) discuss longer-term quota limits or scheduled-job detection to avoid future spikes. I'm going to hand off to sam for monitoring for the next 25m.

sam: taking over monitoring. I will alert if any metric worsens. adding quick check below to run every 5m: 

```bash
# quick health check for the org
curl -s https://telemetry.redwood.internal/api/orgs/neptune-analytics/metrics | jq '.errors_5xx, .token_qps'
```

ops-bot: METRICS SNAPSHOT: pre-change errors_5xx=12.3% token_qps=68 -> post-change errors_5xx=1.6% token_qps=22 (timestamp 1782123590).

ashley: handing off -sam is now primary. I'll be available if needed. Postmortem owner: jordan. ETA for postmortem doc: EOD tomorrow.

sam: noted. I'll extend throttle if we see another spike. If customer asks for immediate resumption, confirm they finish/disable the nightly job.

leah: support will coordinate with the customer and confirm before we fully remove overrides.

jordan: adding action items for postmortem: 
- root cause: why job started now and if streaming/long-seq usage wasn't rate-limited earlier
- missing guardrails: scheduled-job detection, per-org long-seq caps, smarter backpressure
- owner: jordan (prod) + sam (sre) + ashley (runtime)

ashley: closing the pager for now. keeping thread open for updates. will update last_message_ts when resolved. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: NOTE: override cfg-3f9b will auto-expire at +15m unless extended.

sam: extending throttle by 15m to be safe (applying now).

ops-bot: CONFIG UPDATE: extended override cfg-3f9b ttl -> 30m by sam (change-id: cfg-3f9b-ext).

leah: customer confirmed they paused the job and will reschedule. they requested a short summary of actions. I'll draft and send.

sam: monitoring looks stable for last 9m. No regressions.

ashley: thanks team. finishing handoff notes in oncall doc.

jordan: postmortem owner will open doc tomorrow and include suggested mitigations (auto-throttle for unexpected sustained long sequences, scheduled-job detection, per-org streaming disable opt-out).

ops-bot: INCIDENT STATUS -> mitigated. active controls: override cfg-3f9b (qps=20,bust=60 ttl remaining ~18m), safeguard sg-78aa (reject >1500 tokens ttl remaining ~6m).

sam: last check: token QPS 18, errors_5xx 0.7%. I'll drop a final sign-off in ~20m then close the incident thread.

ashley: final: if anything else pops we re-open. postmortem will include timeline and follow-ups. thanks all. :pray:
